### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. orofaciodigital syndrome 20  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.444)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8873719)

**Proposed mechanism:** RAB23 (HGNC:9788) —DISRUPTS→ Basolateral membrane protein targeting (GO:0031599); RAB34 (HGNC:9791) —DISRUPTS→ Basolateral membrane protein targeting (GO:0031599); Basolateral membrane protein targeting (GO:0031599) —LEADS_TO→ Craniosynostosis (HP:0005409); Basolateral membrane protein targeting (GO:0031599) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial shape (HP:0001999); Basolateral membrane protein targeting (GO:0031599) —LEADS_TO→ Oligodactyly (HP:0009002); Basolateral membrane protein targeting (GO:0031599) —LEADS_TO→ Preaxial polydactyly (HP:0009005). Loss-of-function mutations in RAB23 (Carpenter syndrome) and RAB34 (orofaciodigital syndrome 20) converge on the shared pathway of basolateral membrane protein targeting. Impairment of this pathway disrupts essential cellular functions required for proper craniofacial and limb development, leading to the overlapping phenotypes of craniosynostosis, abnormal facial shape, and digital anomalies.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that RAB23 and RAB34 function in completely independent cellular pathways with no overlap in protein trafficking or localization, or identification of distinct, non-overlapping sets of downstream targets critical for development. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.1%) in the coding regions of RAB23 and RAB34 that are not associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of RAB23 and RAB34 in basolateral membrane protein targeting could reveal common therapeutic targets for developmental syndromes caused by defects in this pathway. Strategies aimed at modulating vesicle trafficking or correcting protein localization could potentially benefit patients with either Carpenter syndrome or OFDS20.
